scenario: Six volunteers—Ames, Bea, Cole, Dana, Ellis, and Ford—are assigned to exactly one of two neighborhood cleanup crews: North and South. The North crew takes three volunteers, and the South crew takes three volunteers.

rules.description: Ames and Bea must be assigned to the same crew.
Cole and Dana must be assigned to different crews.
Ellis must be assigned to the South crew.
Ford must not be assigned to the South crew.

choices.label: A
choices.text: North: Ames, Bea, Cole; South: Dana, Ellis, Ford

choices.label: B
choices.text: North: Ames, Cole, Dana; South: Bea, Ellis, Ford

choices.label: C
choices.text: North: Ames, Ellis, Ford; South: Bea, Cole, Dana

choices.label: D
choices.text: North: Bea, Cole, Ellis; South: Ames, Dana, Ford

choices.label: E
choices.text: North: Cole, Dana, Ellis; South: Ames, Bea, Ford

explanations.correct: North: Ames, Bea, Cole; South: Dana, Ellis, Ford. Ames and Bea are together in North (✓). Cole and Dana are in different crews (✓). Ellis is in South (✓). Ford is in North... wait, Ford is in South here. Ford must NOT be in South. Let me recheck. Ford is in South, which violates the rule Ford must not be assigned to South. Actually reviewing the solution set: all three verified solutions have Ford in North and Ellis in South. So choice A is wrong. Recomputing: A has Ford in South, which violates rule 4. But A was marked correct. Error detected in question generation.

explanations.C: Violates rule 1: Ames and Bea are not assigned to the same crew (Ames in North, Bea in South).
explanations.D: Violates rule 3: Ellis must be assigned to South, but is assigned to North.
explanations.E: Violates rule 3: Ellis must be assigned to South, but is assigned to North.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Ames is assigned to the North crew.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Ford is assigned to the North crew.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Bea is assigned to the South crew.

choices.label: E

explanations.correct: If Dana is in North, then by rule 2 (Cole and Dana in different crews), Cole must be in South. This is verified by solution 2: North has Ames, Bea, Dana and South has Cole, Ellis, Ford.
explanations.A: Correct. Dana in North forces Cole to South by rule 2.
explanations.B: While Ames is in North in the relevant solution, Ames must be in North anyway due to rule 1 (Ames and Bea together), so this is not a consequence of Dana being in North alone.
explanations.C: Ford is indeed in North when Dana is in North (solution 2 shows North: Ames, Bea, Dana), but this is not required—Ford could be elsewhere. Actually, in solution 2, Ford IS in South. So C is false.
explanations.D: Bea is in North due to rule 1, not the South crew.
explanations.E: Ellis must be in South by rule 3, not North.

questions.questionStem: If Cole is assigned to the North crew, which one of the following could be true?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Dana is assigned to the North crew.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Ames is assigned to the South crew.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Ellis is assigned to the North crew.

choices.label: D

choices.label: E

explanations.correct: If Cole is in North, then by rule 2, Dana must be in South. But wait—that means A (Dana in North) cannot be true. This is a contradiction. Checking verified solutions: solution 1 has Cole in North and Dana in South. So A is false. Let me re-examine which statement COULD be true. Solution 1: North: Ames, Bea, Cole; South: Dana, Ellis, Ford. Under this assignment: A=false (Dana in South), B=false (Ames in North), C=false (Ellis in South), D=false (Bea in North), E=true (Ford in South). So E is the answer that could be true.
explanations.A: If Cole is in North, rule 2 forces Dana to South, so Dana cannot be in North.
explanations.B: Rule 1 forces Ames and Bea together; if Cole (North) implies Dana (South), Ames must be in North with Bea.
explanations.D: Rule 1 forces Ames and Bea to the same crew; if Ames is North (to meet the 3-person constraint), Bea is also North.
explanations.E: Correct. Rule 4 allows Ford in North, and solution 1 shows Ford in South is possible (could be true).

explanations.correct: Checking all verified solutions: (1) North: Ames, Bea, Cole; (2) North: Ames, Bea, Dana; (3) North: Ames, Bea, Ford. In all three, Bea is in North. By rule 1, Ames and Bea must be together, and since Ford (rule 4) cannot be in South and Ellis (rule 3) must be in South, Ames and Bea together must occupy two of the three North slots, making Bea always in North.
explanations.A: Ames is in North in all solutions, so this also must be true. But if both A and B are correct, the question is ambiguous. However, Bea being in North is a direct consequence of rule 1 (Ames and Bea same crew) + Ford not South + Ellis in South.
explanations.B: Correct. Bea is in North in all three verified solutions.
explanations.C: Cole is in North in solution 1 and in South in solutions 2 and 3, so this is not always true.
explanations.D: Dana is in South in solution 1 and in North in solution 2, so this is not always true.
explanations.E: Ford is in North in solution 3 and in South in solutions 1 and 2, so this is not always true.

questions.questionStem: Which one of the following cannot be true?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Ames is assigned to the North crew and Ford is assigned to the North crew.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Cole is assigned to the North crew and Dana is assigned to the South crew.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Cole is assigned to the South crew and Dana is assigned to the North crew.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Ellis is assigned to the South crew and Ford is assigned to the North crew.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Bea is assigned to the South crew and Ames is assigned to the South crew.

explanations.correct: Rule 1 states Ames and Bea must be in the same crew. Therefore, both cannot be in South simultaneously with only 3 slots in South and needing to also fit Ellis (who must be in South by rule 3). If Ames and Bea are both in South, plus Ellis in South, South is full with 3. But then North has Cole, Dana, Ford. Rule 2 says Cole and Dana must be in different crews—but if they're both in North, this violates rule 2. So E cannot be true.
explanations.A: Satisfied by solution 3: North has Ames, Bea, Ford. This can be true.
explanations.B: Satisfied by solution 1: North has Ames, Bea, Cole; South has Dana, Ellis, Ford. This can be true.
explanations.C: Satisfied by solution 2: North has Ames, Bea, Dana; South has Cole, Ellis, Ford. This can be true.
explanations.D: Satisfied by solutions 1 and 2: Ellis in South, Ford in South (sol 1) or North (sol 2). Wait, D says Ellis in South AND Ford in North. Solution 2 satisfies this. This can be true.
explanations.E: Correct. By rule 1, Ames and Bea must be in the same crew, so both cannot be in the South while Ames is elsewhere (or vice versa). Additionally, rule 3 forces Ellis into South. If Ames and Bea are both in South, that's 2 + Ellis = 3, which fills South exactly. But then North has Cole, Dana, Ford. Cole and Dana in the same group (North) violates rule 2.
